[R732] NEGATIVE - exact head 1be824fccbda5d3341737f5fe033d60edd27af57

Review of processor issue #203 / PR #209, round R732-1. Tree: `ab055c2107ab5ce1ead0f1fa6cfce10ae0956c12`; base: `f65c8ff7c673aaa8e2ea8da654f081ddb13588d8`. One MAJOR remains open. The ordinary REBOOT checks and all selected standing mutants pass their respective gates, but the processor transmits unsolicited responses after ENTITY_DEPARTING and the held reset request.

The independent verdict and five-lens ledger were recorded in [independent-verdict.txt](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/independent-verdict.txt) before querying prior public findings. No other reviewer's report was consulted. The public PR comments contained review-start notices; review submissions and inline threads were empty. There were therefore no prior public FINDINGS to resolve or retain at this head. See [public-pr-comments.json](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/public-pr-comments.json) and [prior-review-query.json](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/prior-review-query.json).

**F1 — MAJOR — terminal shutdown does not close control-plane transmission.** Attributable lenses: **Conformance, RTL, Robustness, Tests, Docs**.

- **Locations:** `hdl/top/protocol_processor_top.sv:4899`–the notification wait and terminal state; `:4667`–the unsolicited TX request remains enabled; `hdl/aecp/KL_aecp_engine.sv:2939`–unsolicited jobs remain admissible; `hdl/aecp/KL_aecp_notify.sv:1428`–automatic unlock generates new notification work. The coverage gap is `tb/pp_top/sim_main.cpp:12613`. The contradicted claim is `docs/guides/integrator.md:697`, “nothing left to send,” and the operator REBOOT row at `docs/guides/operator.md:52`.
- **Authority:** explicit review acceptance item (3), “no further control-plane transmission after DEPARTING,” and the documented issue #203 / REQ-FWX-001 terminal shutdown contract. The sequence's cited authorities are IEEE 1722.1-2021 §7.4.43, §7.5.2, §6.2.4–6.2.6 and Milan v1.2 §5.6.3.5.8/.11. The specific rejection is a missing terminal TX gate under that acceptance condition; it does not infer a blanket SRP/MAAP prohibition from those clauses alone.
- **Evidence:** the unchanged RBT6 stimulus locks the entity, registers three controllers, sends the holder's REBOOT, and delays reset. An observation-only addition counts *every* completed frame after the last DEPARTING. DEPARTING completes at cycle **268095**; `reboot_req_o` rises at **268097**. Three unsolicited AECP responses with opcode **0x0001 (LOCK_ENTITY)** complete at **305144**, **305310**, and **305476**, while the request remains asserted. These are the automatic-unlock notifications; the test wrapper compresses the lock timeout to 400 ms. No new stimulus or RTL change was needed. [Raw probe log](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/post-departure-probe.log), [portable testbench patch](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/post-departure-probe.patch), [positive control](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/reboot-control.log).
- **Impact:** an integrator delaying reset for persistence, or leaving the request unconnected as explicitly documented, sees the supposedly departed control plane transmit again. The current RBT6 checks reject selected command responses and new ADP advertisements, but do not reject these later unsolicited frames. The guide's silence claim is consequently a behavioral error, not wording residue.
- **Required outcome:** after the required SUCCESS response and registered-controller notifications, complete the final DEPARTING and enter a terminal transmission-quiescent state until reset. Cover every producer and preserve frame integrity and the held request; do not suppress the required shutdown frames.
- **Verification:** add an all-frame assertion spanning final DEPARTING through a delayed reset. Exercise lock expiry, asynchronous notifications, pending work, and autonomous transmit producers. A planted defect reopening a producer or terminal gate must fail it. Preserve RBT's status, ordering, backpressure and held-level checks.

**F2 — RESIDUE — the new port comment omits its requirement ID.** Attributable lenses: **Docs, RTL**. Location: `hdl/top/protocol_processor_top.sv:823`. The new block explains behavior and reason and cites issue #203, but omits the requirement ID required by the owner's 2026-10-15 source-comment rule. Exact fix: change its heading to `//! ---- REBOOT request (REQ-FWX-001; IEEE 1722.1-2021 §7.4.43; issue #203) ----`. This adds only a comment reference; no behavior, measurement, verdict, test, figure, generated artifact or clause claim changes. Verify the heading and a comment-only diff. This residue does not affect lens cleanliness. No new bench-lane name, reviewer ID or review-round provenance was identified in the added production HDL comments.

The remaining reviewed behavior is supported as follows:

| Check | Artifact-specific assessment |
|---|---|
| Descriptor/status routing | `KL_aecp_engine.sv:3653` and `gen_ucode.py:2351`: short command → BAD_ARGUMENTS; non-ENTITY type → NOT_SUPPORTED; ENTITY locate miss → NO_SUCH_DESCRIPTOR; foreign lock → ENTITY_LOCKED; otherwise SUCCESS. RBT1–4 grade the response bytes and continued service after refusals. These match the frozen issue's explicit status list. The prompt's NOT_IMPLEMENTED alternative is not silently substituted for that list; the precise external table interpretation remains a primary-source limitation below. |
| Lock/acquire | E_RBOOT runs locate then CHECK_LOCK. RBT4 rejects the non-owner; RBT6 accepts the holder. RBT5 and the existing ACQUIRE_ENTITY path demonstrate NOT_SUPPORTED, so no acquire owner is created under the documented Milan §5.4.2.1 profile. |
| Response, notifications, departure | RBT6 observes SUCCESS, one REBOOT notification to each other registered controller, no requester notification, then DEPARTING, then the request. RBT7 stalls the SUCCESS EOF and proves the request stays low. RBT8 covers a padded command and no advertisement. The engine's serialized response path prevents its REBOOT unsolicited jobs from preceding that response. |
| Held request | `RB_REQ` has no outgoing normal transition; synchronous active-low reset clears it. Engine admission hold and whole-frame RX gating persist. The finite delayed-reset observation sees no request fall. F1 concerns continuing TX, not a request pulse. |
| Scope/interface | Only `reboot_req_o` is added at the production top; no top-level parameter or register-map change. Interface F02.10 and the guide unambiguously specify a held level, reset clearing, MAC EOF handshake and persistence responsibility. They do not specify a reset implementation here. [Parent issue #787](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/787) owns that implementation and its bound. F1 makes the documented quiet interval false; it does not make the output's electrical/temporal contract ambiguous. |
| Models/docs | Reviewed the command-model row, generated decode changes, sweep restart after successful REBOOT, requirement/gap updates, architecture changes, both guides, bench READMEs and PR body. Diagram 21 was rendered and visually inspected. Documentation gates pass; they do not detect F1. |

Independent executable results, all on disposable copies of this exact source:

| Execution | Result / receipt |
|---|---|
| Focused REBOOT positive control | **79 checks, 0 failures**; [reboot-control.log](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/reboot-control.log) |
| Observation-only post-departure probe | **80 checks, 1 failure**, expected defect demonstration; [post-departure-probe.log](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/post-departure-probe.log) |

| Four recut AECP patches, including both uses of SET_CONFIGURATION barrier patch | **5/5 uses KILLED**, all three controls PASS; failure counts and named checks match the published run; [recut-aecp.log](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/recut-aecp.log) |
| Two recut ADP patches | **2/2 KILLED**, both interface controls PASS; counts match the published run; [recut-adp.log](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/recut-adp.log) |
| Both changed D3 substitutions | **2/2 KILLED**, golden PASS; `dispatch_not_held` still kills D3O1 and `enable_not_released_by_restore` still kills D3R1/D3C6; [results](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/recut-d3/results.json) |
| Documentation gates | **PASS**, including 231/231 command-model planted defects; [docs-check-git.log](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/docs-check-git.log) |
| Source and receipt audit | **736 tracked blobs, modes and index entries match**; no tracked diff; **no submodule gitlinks exist in this processor tree**; 11 selected public receipts match their published SHA-256; [audit.log](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/audit.log) |

The six recut patches preserve their original planted behavior: collapsed ADP egress selection, live rather than latched ingress selection, READ_DESCRIPTOR treated as a global barrier, deadline kill tied off, SET_CONFIGURATION downgraded from barrier, and the old hazard classifier stub restored. Both D3 edits remove only the restore-related guard while preserving the newly added REBOOT guard. The retired `a5b-reboot-success-arm` is appropriately replaced: SUCCESS for ENTITY 0 is now intentional. Each of the 17 new README mutation rows has a real patch and a completed named failure, not a compile failure counted as a kill.

Public evidence was read from the [pinned evidence tree](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/tree/abbe89c77cf48311f553592dab7c66f1687c27cc/review-evidence/pp203-r1), after the independent diff pass. Its exact-head source sweep reports **1,030,845 checks, zero failures**. Earlier mutation receipts are at `5fd298c`, with ADP receipts at `061a9ec`; the reviewed history confirms that subsequent relevant source differences are documentation only (the intervening D3 driver edit is separately covered). These are **author source receipts**, not manager source-bank runs. No manager source bank is asserted or inferred.

The [hosted run](https://github.com/Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan/actions/runs/40913411723) was still in progress at the final run query. The inspected jobs showed documentation and portability completed successfully; suites were running. The simulator-build step was **skipped** because of the cached build, and later suite/campaign steps were pending. Skipped/pending steps are not execution evidence. See [hosted-jobs.json](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/hosted-jobs.json) and [hosted-run-final.json](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/hosted-run-final.json).

Limits and pending duties:

- Repository AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md were absent. The supplied AGENTS instruction was followed. The documentation guide, frozen issue acceptance and public assignment were read before the independent source pass. Full licensed IEEE and Milan PDFs were not available in the clone; public download attempts failed or returned only a preview. Clause references were reconstructed from the frozen scope and repository/public citations, not independently verified against complete primary PDFs. In particular, this report does **not** provide a final normative endorsement of NOT_SUPPORTED versus NOT_IMPLEMENTED for every unsupported descriptor target. Obtain that primary-text check before a positive conformance disposition.
- No full processor/parent/gPTP/synthesis/builder bank, route, hardware or physical calibration was run. **Physical calibration NOT RUN**; field skips and digital simulations are not hardware proof. Multi-interface ADP recut checks passed, but this review did not execute a separate multi-interface REBOOT sequence.
- The initial archive-based documentation attempt lacked Git metadata; it was rerun successfully in a detached clone. An initial D3 attempt selected the default 5.052 build and escaped the intended aggregate concurrency bound; it was stopped and discarded, then rerun explicitly with the pinned 5.050 wrapper. Accepted receipts use the pinned version. Observed unit peak memory was 8,931,160,064 bytes, below 12 GiB. Details and the incidental process-listing limitation are in [EXECUTION.txt](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/EXECUTION.txt).

Parent reset wiring, persistence policy, pin adoption edits and physical reset/recovery proof remain in #787 and its release gates. Resolve F1 and obtain the required independent positive reviews before merge.

[run-focused.py](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/run-focused.py), [run-recuts.py](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/run-recuts.py) and [audit.py](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/b667f78fdca98787745e1c8f5996df35503f4df0/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-1/audit.py) accept the source checkout as their argument; the first creates the bounded compiler wrapper used by the second. `REVIEW_VERILATOR` can override the first script's pinned executable path. [R732] NEGATIVE - exact head ec1ff275a72d885f0908fd213d8009e9e4dda4d9

Issue #203 / PR #209, round R732-2. Tree `be6818cf5ccccf5d327cc43adaec34c1df51b98c`; source base `f65c8ff7c673aaa8e2ea8da654f081ddb13588d8`; delta from `1be824fccbda5d3341737f5fe033d60edd27af57`. One MAJOR and one MINOR remain open. The original post-DEPARTING leak is fixed, but a non-advertising entity can raise its reset request during another producer's frame. The live PR presents superseded validation measurements as current.

The independent verdict and ledger are recorded in [independent-verdict.txt](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/95ef1fda641e7fd17e5b75643f1d1941b08af413/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-2/independent-verdict.txt). No other reviewer's report was read. The prior public R732-1 findings were consulted only after the independent diff pass. Public review submissions and inline comments were empty; the conversation contained the R732-1 findings and review-start notices ([public-pr-comments.json](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/95ef1fda641e7fd17e5b75643f1d1941b08af413/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-2/public-pr-comments.json), [public-reviews.json](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/95ef1fda641e7fd17e5b75643f1d1941b08af413/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-2/public-reviews.json), [public-inline-comments.json](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/95ef1fda641e7fd17e5b75643f1d1941b08af413/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-2/public-inline-comments.json)).

**Prior findings**

- **R732-F1, MAJOR — RESOLVED at its named post-DEPARTING cause.** The common request mask at `hdl/top/protocol_processor_top.sv:4689` and `:4920` closes non-ADP arbitration once ADP finishes building. ADP's effective enable remains low. The exact published observation-only [probe patch](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/95ef1fda641e7fd17e5b75643f1d1941b08af413/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-2/post-departure-probe.patch) applies and passes: **128 checks, zero failures**, including its all-frame assertion ([log](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/95ef1fda641e7fd17e5b75643f1d1941b08af413/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-2/post-departure-probe.log), [return code](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/95ef1fda641e7fd17e5b75643f1d1941b08af413/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-2/post-departure-probe.rc)). The exact-head control passes **127 checks**. RBT9–11 additionally exercise delayed reset, live producer requests, EOF backpressure and slot exhaustion. The separate no-DEPARTING edge F3 prevents an overall clean terminal-state disposition.
- **R732-F2, RESIDUE — RESOLVED.** `hdl/top/protocol_processor_top.sv:824` now reads `REBOOT request (REQ-FWX-001; IEEE 1722.1-2021 §7.4.43; issue #203)`. Commit `aede92e` makes the requested comment-only correction. No new prohibited bench-lane label, reviewer identifier or review-round provenance was found in the delta's source comments.

**R732-F3 — MAJOR — reset request precedes completion of a non-ADP frame when no DEPARTING is required.**

**Attributable lenses:** Conformance, RTL, Robustness, Tests, Docs.

**Locations:** `hdl/top/protocol_processor_top.sv:4920–4940`, particularly the `RB_DEP` exit at `:4938`; `hdl/packet_engine/KL_pp_tx_arbiter.sv` selection/start/stream lifecycle; `tb/pp_top/sim_main.cpp:12737` (RBT8). Contradicted interface statements: `docs/architecture/02_interfaces.md:582` and `docs/guides/integrator.md:697`. `docs/architecture/06_aecp_engine.md:1127–1129` acknowledges that a frame selected in the closing interval can still go, without reconciling that with the request's unconditional silence contract.

**Authority/evidence:** issue #203's terminal transmit-quiet and frame-integrity acceptance, [public round-two scope decision](https://github.com/Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan/issues/203#issuecomment-6503153894), REQ-FWX-001, and F02.10's explicit promise that nothing leaves `tx_*` from the request's rise until reset. This finding rests on that project/interface contract, not an inferred blanket ACMP prohibition from an IEEE clause.

The [portable probe](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/95ef1fda641e7fd17e5b75643f1d1941b08af413/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-2/nonadvertising-probe.patch) uses real interfaces and unchanged RTL. It boots with advertising disabled, raises link-up, registers one other controller, binds eight sinks to a discovered talker and takes the lock. It holds the required REBOOT notification's EOF for 5 seconds, as RBT11 does, leaving every standard TX slot occupied. It then releases the notification and withholds reset. SUCCESS and the required notification complete; no DEPARTING is generated, as appropriate. The request rises at cycle **16184473**, with a frame already in progress (`in_frame=1`, one byte collected, `tx_valid_o=1`). An autonomous ACMP frame, subtype `0xFC`, message `0x00`, finishes at **16184542**, **69 cycles after the request**. The suite reports **134 checks, one failure**, solely the new no-byte-after-request assertion ([raw log](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/95ef1fda641e7fd17e5b75643f1d1941b08af413/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-2/nonadvertising-probe.log), [return code](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/95ef1fda641e7fd17e5b75643f1d1941b08af413/review-evidence/pp203-r1/reviews/R732-2/nonadvertising-probe.rc)). The held-request and legitimate no-advertising shutdown checks pass.

**Cause/impact:** the gate prevents future arbitration but preserves a selected frame. `RB_DEP` waits only for ADP's builder, queue and flight. With ADP already down, those conditions are empty while another producer's frame selected during shutdown can remain active. The new terminal gate depends on a final ADP frame to establish whole-plane drainage. An integrator resetting immediately on the documented request can interrupt that active frame; an integrator delaying reset observes transmission during the promised quiet interval. This dependency and the strengthened interface claim are directly affected by the delta.

**Required outcome:** establish terminal silence before asserting the request even without a DEPARTING. Close further admission and account for every already selected or active frame across all producers, preserving frame integrity, required SUCCESS/notifications, advertised shutdown ordering and the held request. Reconcile the interface and guide statements with the implemented guarantee.

**Verification:** retain RBT1–11 and the original reviewer probe. Add a non-advertising shutdown with autonomous work queued behind a held notification; check every offered byte from the request through delayed reset. Hold the selected non-ADP frame at EOF and require the request to stay low until completion. A plant removing that whole-plane completion condition must fail. RBT8 currently supplies no competing autonomous work; RBT9–11 exercise advertising and miss this edge.

**R732-F4 — MINOR — live PR validation claims still describe round one.**

# R731-1 independent review: processor issue #203 / PR #209 (AECP REBOOT)

- Repository: Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan, PR #209
- Exact head: `ec1ff275a72d885f0908fd213d8009e9e4dda4d9`, tree `be6818cf5ccccf5d327cc43adaec34c1df51b98c`
- Source base: `f65c8ff7`. Delta reviewed: `git diff f65c8ff7..ec1ff275` (12 commits, 63 files)
- Reviewer: internal independent reviewer, cleared context, own detached clone
- Simulator for every executed receipt: the scoped Verilator 5.050 (`Verilator 5.050 2026-07-01 rev v5.050`)

## Verdict

NEGATIVE, on one open MAJOR (R731-F1). When the entity is not advertising, `reboot_req_o`
rises while a frame from another lane is still on `tx_*`. That breaks the port's defining
contract (02 F02.10: "From its rise to `rst_n` nothing leaves on `tx_*`"). An integrator who
follows the guide and drives `rst_n` from the request then cuts that frame mid-transmission.
The advertising path, the response/notification/DEPARTING ordering, the status table, the lock
interaction, the RX and engine holds, and the transmit gate after the final DEPARTING all hold.
All 30 RBT arms and all 8 re-cut arms are KILLED by name at this head.

## Findings

### R731-F1 (MAJOR): a non-advertising REBOOT raises `reboot_req_o` while a frame is still on `tx_*`

- **Lenses:** RTL, Robustness, Tests.
- **Where:** `hdl/top/protocol_processor_top.sv:4905` (`rbt_tx_flight` tracks only the
  unsolicited-AECP and ADP lanes) and `hdl/top/protocol_processor_top.sv:4938`-`4940` (RB_DEP
  leaves on ADP's builder, ADP's lane queue and ADP's flight only).
- **Authority:**
  - 02 F02.10 (`docs/architecture/02_interfaces.md:582`): "It rises only after ... From its rise
    to `rst_n` nothing leaves on `tx_*`".
  - The port contract (`hdl/top/protocol_processor_top.sv:824`-`846`): "three things have left
    the transmit path ... a reset held back finds the entity silent".
  - Integrator guide bring-up step 7 (`docs/guides/integrator.md:697`-`702`): "the processor
    sends nothing more ... transmitting no frame, for your `rst_n`". The same guide, at line 31,
    says to drive `rst_n` from the request.
  - Operator guide (`docs/guides/operator.md:52`): "then nothing ... sends no frame".
  - The round-2 required outcome on the issue: a terminal transmit-quiet state in which "frame
    integrity and the held request are kept".
- **Mechanism:**
  - RB_NTF ends at the last REBOOT notification's last byte.
  - In the same clocks the idle arbiter may select any request already waiting, because the gate
    is still open. Examples are the lock's automatic-unlock notification (not command work, so
    `cmd_busy_o` does not cover it), a listener probe, MAAP and SRP.
  - With no advertise machine up, RB_DOWN and RB_DEP pass in one clock each. RB_DEP sees ADP idle,
    and `reboot_req_o` rises about three clocks after that frame's grant.
  - The frame is at least 64 bytes and still streams for tens of clocks. Nothing waits for a
    frame of a lane other than ADP or unsolicited AECP.
  - In the advertising case the same frame always goes before the DEPARTING, and RB_DEP waits for
    the DEPARTING's flight, so that path is safe.
  - The prepared round-2 PR body states the window ("a frame granted in those two clocks still
    goes"). It does not state that this frame overlaps the request.
- **Evidence:** `receipts/probe_window.log`, from the probe
  `probes/window-after-notification-round.patch` (a scenario added to a scratch copy of
  `tb/pp_top/sim_main.cpp`, run by `scripts/run_window_probe.sh`). The scenario is: one other
  controller registered, the requester holds the lock, and the MAC holds the REBOOT
  notification's last byte for 1 s so that the lock expires.
  - Not advertising (`PRB-NA`): `reboot_req_o` rose at clock 105454. The unsolicited
    LOCK_ENTITY (command_type 0x0001, u = 1) to the other controller took its last byte at
    105513, 59 clocks later.
  - The same scenario advertising (`PRB-ADV`) passes. The SRP frame and the DEPARTING both
    leave before the rise.
  - No RBT row covers a non-advertising REBOOT with a second producer live. RBT7 and RBT8 are
    the only non-advertising rows, and they run with nothing else to send.
- **Impact:** a reset taken on the request truncates a frame at the MAC boundary: a frame with
  no `tx_eof_o`. What the MAC FIFO then does (a runt, a bad-FCS frame, or a wedged FIFO) is the
  integrator's MAC's. The request no longer means "nothing more on `tx_*`", which is the one
  property the guide asks the integrator to rely on.
- **Required outcome:** `reboot_req_o` rises only when the transmit gate is closed and no frame
  of any lane is in flight. For example, RB_DEP (or a final state) also waits for the arbiter
  to be idle with no grant outstanding, on every path, advertising or not.
  - Add an RBT row: not advertising, a second producer live in the clocks the notification round
    ends (the lock-expiry stimulus above suffices). It asserts that the last byte offered on
    `tx_*` precedes the rise.
  - Add a named arm that removes the new wait and is killed by that row.
  - RBT1 to RBT11 and the round's arms stay KILLED.
  - The PR body's two-clock sentence is updated to match.
- **Verification:** `scripts/run_window_probe.sh <exact-head tree> <verilator>` passes both
  `PRB-NA` and `PRB-ADV`. `make -C tb/pp_top reboot` shows 0 failures. The REBOOT arms in
  `aecp_dispatch_mutants.py`, the new one included, are all KILLED by name.

### R731-S1 (SUGGESTION): state the request's clock-domain contract, or register it

- **Lenses:** RTL, Docs.
- **Where:** `hdl/top/protocol_processor_top.sv:4949` and `docs/guides/integrator.md:31`.
- **Observation:**
  - `reboot_req_o` is a combinational decode (`rbt_st_r == RB_REQ`) of a binary-encoded 3-bit
    state register.
  - The RB_DOWN to RB_DEP step is 011 to 100. In gates it can decode as 101 for a moment, unless
    synthesis re-encodes the machine.
  - Inside `clk_i` this is harmless. But the guide says to drive `rst_n` from the request "by
    whatever reset your end station uses", and an asynchronous reset input would see that pulse
    before the DEPARTING has left.
  - The general rule that class-D outputs are combinational reads of `clk_i`-domain registers
    (`docs/guides/integrator.md:46`) covers it only by implication.
  - Nor does the contract say whether a one-clock synchronous reset taken straight from the
    request is enough.
- **Suggested outcome:** register `reboot_req_o` (one flop), or state at F02.10 and in the
  guide that it is a `clk_i`-domain output to be sampled synchronously, with the minimum
  `rst_n` assertion. This answers focus item (6). The parent's use of the port is milan-fpga
  #787, and the contract leaves this point to it.

### R731-S2 (SUGGESTION): the whole-frame RX discard has no observable test

- **Lenses:** Tests.
- **Where:** `hdl/top/protocol_processor_top.sv` `rx_reboot_gate`.
- **Observation:** probe `p2-rx-gate-cuts-mid-frame` cuts the frame that is arriving at the
  acceptance (`rx_take_w = rx_valid_i && !aecp_reboot_w`). It SURVIVED, with RBT at 127 checks
  and 0 failures. The prefix it leaves in the validator never completes, and nothing after it is

     response's A_TXW grant. RBT6 checks the order. CONFORMS.
2. **Order** (§7.5.2, Milan v1.2 §5.4.5.2; IEEE §6.2.4/§6.2.5.2.2, Milan §5.6.3.5.8/.11).
   - The order is response, then notifications to every other registered controller (none to
     the requester), then ENTITY_DEPARTING, then `reboot_req_o` (RBT6, RBT9).
   - ADP's `enable_fall_w` is combinational on its input, so RB_DOWN's single clock sets
     `pend_dep_r` before RB_DEP reads `tx_busy_o`.
   - B_REQ hands to the lane queue on the same edge the builder goes idle, so RB_DEP has no gap
     between the two (probes p3 and p5 confirm both waits matter). CONFORMS for the advertising
     path. See R731-F1 for the non-advertising path's overlap with another lane's frame.
3. **Held, one-way request; silence after DEPARTING.**
   - RB_REQ has no exit. RBT6, RBT9 and RBT10 grade the hold.
   - The arbiter mask `arb_req_w = arb_want_w & rbt_tx_open_w` affects only selection: a lane
     selected before the gate closes is granted and sent before the queued DEPARTING. After the
     final DEPARTING nothing is offered on `tx_*` through a 75 s or 65 s withheld reset (RBT9,
     RBT10), and nothing follows when every slot is taken (RBT11).
   - Probes p1 (the gate reopening at RB_REQ), p4 (the gate at RB_DEP's entry) and p6 (the
     request dropped on RX) are each DETECTED.
